chapter_note: This chapter is predominantly later editorial material — a homiletic structure using cosmological narrative (light's unity vs. darkness's disunity) as a springboard for worldly analogy and community exhortation. Teaching purity is 0.000; no systematic correspondential mapping (zoomorphic, metal, taste, five-element) is present. Paragraphs 1-3 contain cosmological narrative fragments where both sides stay within the cosmic system (light entities, dark powers, abyss, disunity), but these are simple cosmological principles rather than the systematic domain-mapping characteristic of the strongest substrate chapters. Paragraphs 4-8 are entirely editorial bridge and exhortation. The possible Gospel echo ('kingdom divided within itself', cf. Mark 3:24) in paragraph 3 adds uncertainty. Heavy lacunae in paragraphs 1-2 obscure the original structure. Overall, this chapter preserves at best fragments of old cosmological teaching, heavily wrapped in editorial application.

paragraphs.core_text: [Now as to what affects the] light, behold, at the beginning the Darkness was strong against it; [ ... ] no disunity [ ... ] exists in the light.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame formula: 'Once again the enlightener speaks to his disciples:'
paragraphs.temporal_note: Frame formula is standard dialogue layer. The cosmological assertion — Darkness strong against light at the beginning, no disunity in the light — states a cosmic principle with both sides within the cosmic system. However, this is a simple theological principle rather than systematic correspondential mapping, so substrate classification carries uncertainty.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] how far [ ... the lig]ht that came forth from [ ... ] in that place in a [ ... ] alone [ ... ] ⟨p.128⟩ the greatness of the light with one another for ever, and nor did one of them transgress the command and order that his brother had entrusted to him forever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Heavily lacunose but surviving text describes the internal order of light entities — their mutual harmony, their hierarchical commands, their eternal cooperation. Both sides of the description stay within the cosmic system (light entities, their relationships, their commands). The language 'command and order that his brother had entrusted' describes hierarchical cosmic governance. Uncertainty is high due to lacunae — we cannot see the opening and cannot rule out frame material in the lost sections.

paragraphs.core_text: However, the Darkness, the enemy, was doomed and overcome; because of the arising of disharmony it was divided within itself. Even the kingdom was divided within itself; [and] ev[en] the [powers, who had] left their abyss behind and come up fo[llow-ing] it, were doomed because of the disunity that was present in all of them. The Darkness was destroyed, and its other powers were humiliated
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed editorial bridge clause: 'because the p[ower] of that first light functions in the same way as the kingdom of this world.' This maps cosmic→contemporary ('kingdom of this world' reaches outside the cosmic system into the editor's present) and serves as the hinge connecting cosmological narrative to the worldly analogy in paragraphs 4-5.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The cosmic narrative (darkness overcome by disunity, powers leaving abyss, darkness destroyed) describes events within the cosmic system — both sides stay internal. The final clause ('functions in the same way as the kingdom of this world') is the editorial seam that bridges to the worldly analogy. Note possible Gospel echo in 'kingdom divided within itself' (cf. Mark 3:24), which could indicate editorial shaping of the cosmic narrative, but the concept of a divided dark realm is independently attested in Manichaean cosmology. Uncertainty is genuine.

Entirely worldly kingdom analogy — describes how a kingdom prospers when its associates agree and surpasses rival kingdoms. One side of the mapping (kingdoms, associates, glory, marvel) is outside the cosmic system. This is the editor's illustrative analogy connecting the cosmic principle (light's unity) to worldly experience, preparing for the community exhortation in paragraph 6.

Continuation of the worldly kingdom analogy — the united kingdom condemns and humiliates the divided one. Still entirely outside the cosmic system, describing political dynamics. The vocabulary ('associates in the mystery', 'condemn', 'come under the hand') mirrors paragraph 4 and completes the bridge analogy before the pivot to exhortation.

'In exactly the same way, you yourselves' — bridge connective flagged by the pipeline, correctly. This is the explicit pivot to community application. Direct address ('you yourselves'), reference to 'this living truth that is unveiled to you', and injunction to 'conquer the sin that is set up against you' are all hallmarks of the exhortation layer. The cosmic principle (light's unity defeats darkness) is now APPLIED to the audience's spiritual struggle.

Continued exhortation with escalating emotional register — 'may it not happen!' is a devotional interjection. Direct address, warning about consequences of division ('condemned', 'humiliated under the hand of sin'). The exhortation vocabulary score (6.9) confirms. References to 'this truth that is unveiled to you' mark the community's present experience.

Devotional closure with imperative voice: 'Neither be divided... you will conquer those above and those below; and bring under your feet every thing that is and that will be!' Classic exhortation closure — moral injunction + eschatological promise. The language of triumph ('conquer', 'bring under your feet', 'every thing that is and that will be') is devotional-eschatological, not cosmological-correspondential.
